title: A mutating command should be able to render in the same step

sections.heading: Why
sections.body:
Nothing that mutates state renders. So `slicer done S30` leaves `.slicer/render/` stale,
and the very next `slicer check` fails until `slicer render` is run — every single time.
This session that is 19 done/render/check cycles and 139 mutations; the render step is a
rote extra command after each one, and forgetting it means a red check that looks like a
problem but is just staleness.

    $ slicer done S30
    S30 -> done
    $ slicer check
    stale render: ROADMAP.md
    check failed; run `slicer render` and `slicer sync`, then re-run

sections.heading: Files
sections.body: - `src/slicer/cli.py` — the mutating command handlers, or a shared post-mutation hook

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body:
1. `done --render` leaves the render current, so a following `check` passes with no
   separate `render`.
2. Without the flag, behaviour is unchanged (render stays a separate step).
3. The flag reports what it rendered.

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body:
Add a `--render` flag to the mutating commands (`done`, `park`, `unpark`, `set`, `add`,
`promote`, `move`, `edit`, `remove`) that runs `render.plan`/`compare`/`write` after the
mutation, via one shared helper so the commands cannot drift. Keep render a separate
command too; this only removes the rote second step for the common "mutate then render"
case. Consider whether a config default ("always render after a mutation") is worth it, or
whether the explicit flag is enough — the flag is the smaller, less surprising change.

**Not in this slice:** auto-running `sync` as well; sync targets are project-specific and
rarer, and `check` still names sync drift when it matters.

sections.heading: Check
sections.body: `slicer done S01 --render && slicer check` is clean with no manual render.
